# watchpoint_incident_severity_policy (Resource)

The response contract for one rung of the internal SEV ladder: how fast an incident of that severity must be picked up, who gets paged, and whether it owes a postmortem. This is the engineering severity, separate from the public impact level a status page shows. The ladder is fixed at `Sev1`, `Sev2`, `Sev3`, `Sev4`, so this resource configures a rung that always exists rather than creating one. Attributes left out keep whatever was effective before, which is the built-in default on a rung nobody has customised. Destroying the resource leaves the stored override in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Tighten the top of the ladder: a SEV1 must be picked up in two minutes, pages
# the primary on-call policy, and owes a postmortem within two days.
resource "watchpoint_incident_severity_policy" "sev1" {
  severity                  = "Sev1"
  response_target_minutes   = 2
  require_postmortem        = true
  postmortem_due_hours      = 48
  page_escalation_policy_id = watchpoint_escalation_policy.primary.id
}

# Rungs left alone keep their built-in defaults, so configure only what differs.
# Here SEV3 keeps its 60-minute target and simply starts owing a postmortem.
resource "watchpoint_incident_severity_policy" "sev3" {
  severity             = "Sev3"
  require_postmortem   = true
  postmortem_due_hours = 168
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `severity` (String) Which rung of the ladder this configures: `Sev1`, `Sev2`, `Sev3`, `Sev4`. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `page_escalation_policy_id` (String) ID of the escalation policy paged when an incident of this severity is declared. The policy must belong to this organization. Omit it to page nobody by severity, which is also what removing it from the configuration does.
- `postmortem_due_hours` (Number) How long after resolution the postmortem is due, in hours (1 to 2160). Ignored unless `require_postmortem` is `true`. Built-in defaults are 72 for `Sev1`, 120 for `Sev2` and 168 for `Sev3` and `Sev4`.
- `require_postmortem` (Boolean) Whether resolving an incident of this severity opens a postmortem obligation, which is then reminded on and escalated. Built-in defaults are `true` for `Sev1` and `Sev2`, `false` for `Sev3` and `Sev4`.
- `response_target_minutes` (Number) How long an incident of this severity may go unacknowledged before the response target is breached, in minutes (1 to 10080). Built-in defaults are 5 for `Sev1`, 15 for `Sev2`, 60 for `Sev3` and 240 for `Sev4`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Severity policy ID, which is the severity name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import ID is the severity name: Sev1, Sev2, Sev3 or Sev4.
terraform import watchpoint_incident_severity_policy.sev1 Sev1
```
